dedupe_keys.name: falls lake agent based model critical transitions dataset

description: Emily Berglund at North Carolina State University publishes outputs from the Falls Lake agent-based water-supply model. Four management strategies and 16 climate-shift factors generate 64 scenario settings, each with 100 stochastic simulations. Monthly storage and deficit series use million cubic metres; other columns describe inflow, outflow and water supply. Early-warning indicators use log-transformed reservoir storage with a 25-percent moving window, starting at month 300 of 1,200 timesteps. The August 2020 deposit provides a text-file download as Archive.zip free under CC BY 4.0. These are model outputs for a named reservoir system, not measured operating histories. They can compare drought-management performance or benchmark tipping-point diagnostics across scenario ensembles. The source describes light and severe restrictions, whereas the later diagnostic-code deposit uses reactive and proactive labels; exact scenario equivalence remains uncertain and requires checking. The separate R tipping-point workflow is recorded in G6. No related catalogue record explicitly identifies these outputs, and the archive was not opened.
